heroValue:
Connect field sensors.
Across your site.
heroDescription: The Hitelecom H68 connects compatible LoRa sensors across outdoor facilities to a monitoring platform. An 8-channel full-duplex radio architecture, IP68-rated enclosure and 4G LTE backhaul support distributed monitoring at utility, energy and industrial sites. Use MQTT integration to bring field data into Hitelecom Cloud or a compatible customer platform.

featureIntro: Connect distributed measurement points with a deployment planned for radio coverage, exposure, power and onward data delivery.

features.title: LoRa sensor aggregation
features.text: Collect data from compatible LoRa devices through the published 8-channel full-duplex radio architecture. Match the sensor protocol and regional settings.

features.title: 4G LTE backhaul
features.text: Forward collected data over an available mobile network. Select the modem, SIM and operator around coverage at the gateway position.

features.title: MQTT integration
features.text: Connect field data to Hitelecom Cloud or a compatible customer platform with an agreed endpoint, message format and authentication configuration.

features.title: IP68-rated enclosure
features.text: Plan outdoor mounting, cable entries and connector sealing as one installation. The enclosure rating applies under the specified installation conditions.

features.title: Regional radio options
features.text: Select CN470, EU868, IN865, RU864, US915 or AU915 for the deployment. Frequency, channel settings and transmit power must match the local requirements.

features.title: Site-specific coverage
features.text: Up to 10 km in open-area conditions. Terrain, structures, antenna height and interference determine the usable field coverage.

features.title: Local platform deployment
features.text: A local deployment can be planned for projects that require site-controlled data handling. Agree the server role, connectivity and integration scope.

features.title: Power-loss notification
features.text: A power-loss alert can be transmitted when backup power and the backhaul connection remain available. Include the required alert path in the power design.

faqs.q: What does the H68 gateway do?
faqs.a: The H68 receives data from compatible LoRa sensors and forwards it to a monitoring platform through the configured backhaul. The gateway provides the connection between sensor points and the platform; the connected sensors perform the measurements.

faqs.q: How is the H66 different from the H68?
faqs.a: H66 is positioned for indoor facilities, with an IP65 enclosure, an operating range of −20°C to +70°C and an open-area distance reference of up to 5 km. H68 is positioned for outdoor sites, with an IP68 enclosure, an operating range of −40°C to +85°C and an open-area reference of up to 10 km. Choose by installation conditions and a site-specific radio assessment.

faqs.q: Will one H68 cover the entire site?
faqs.a: Gateway quantity depends on the actual radio paths, antenna positions, interference and sensor traffic. An open-area distance figure cannot establish coverage inside buildings or behind terrain and structures. Share a site plan and representative sensor positions so the network can be assessed and tested.

faqs.q: How many sensors can one gateway connect?
faqs.a: Capacity depends on payload size, reporting interval, radio settings, traffic concentration, retransmissions and downlink requirements. There is no single device-count figure that applies to every deployment. Provide the sensor list and reporting profile for network sizing.

faqs.q: Does LoRa support mean the gateway is LoRaWAN-compatible?
faqs.a: LoRa identifies the radio technology. LoRaWAN is a network protocol with separate device, gateway and server requirements. Confirm the exact sensor protocol, gateway firmware and platform compatibility for any LoRaWAN requirement before selecting the configuration.

faqs.q: Which frequency and cellular bands should I choose?
faqs.a: Select the regional radio configuration for the deployment country and the LTE modem for the local operator. The published regional radio options and LTE bands are listed in the specification table. A regional band name does not establish local certification or universal operator coverage.

faqs.q: Can I use Hitelecom Cloud or my own platform?
faqs.a: Yes. Agree the integration configuration for Hitelecom Cloud or a compatible customer platform. MQTT is listed in the specification. Confirm the endpoint, topics, payload mapping, timestamps, authentication and any required transport security, then verify a sample message end to end.

faqs.q: Can I view readings online and receive threshold alarms?
faqs.a: With the agreed Hitelecom Cloud integration, users can view uploaded monitoring data online and receive alerts when measurements exceed configured thresholds. Sensor sampling, reporting intervals, network availability and platform settings determine when the information is available. Define recipients and the response workflow during commissioning.

faqs.q: What happens during a power failure?
faqs.a: A power-loss notification requires enough backup energy to operate the gateway and a working backhaul connection. It does not mean transmission continues indefinitely after power is removed. Confirm the backup-power arrangement, notification path and required duration for the project.

faqs.q: What does IP68 mean for outdoor installation?
faqs.a: The IP68 rating applies under the specified enclosure test and installation conditions. Plan sealed cable entries, connector protection, mounting, earthing and environmental exposure for the complete assembly. Confirm any immersion depth or duration requirement separately; the rating does not establish explosion protection.
